learning_outcomes.text: Can interpret the effects of atomic structure, crystal structure, and crystal structure defects on material properties.

Can perform calculations for the concept of diffusion, its related laws, temperature-dependent diffusion coefficient, and diffusion time, and interpret the importance (effect) of diffusion in practice.

Relates material behaviors at micro and macro scales. Knows how the mechanical properties of metals are determined and can interpret the results. Knows the material properties affecting mechanical behavior and their determination.
Can interpret types of damage. Knows what affects the properties of an alloy. Knows heat treatment methods. Can select the appropriate process for desired properties.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Materials Science, Classification of Materials
Atomic structure, Interatomic bonds, Effect of bonding properties on physical properties, Crystal structure types.
Crystal Lattice Points, Directions and Planes, Crystalline and non-crystalline materials
Crystal structure defects and their effects, Microscopic examination methods
Diffusion phenomenon, Steady-state Diffusion, Unsteady-state Diffusion
Mechanical properties, Concepts of stress and strain, Elastic deformation, Elastic Properties of Materials
Plastic deformation, Recovery after plastic deformation, True stress true strain
Dislocations and plastic deformation, strengthening mechanisms.
Damage types, Fracture, brittle-ductile transition temperature
Iron-carbon equilibrium diagram and phase transformations
assessment_rules: The overall grade is calculated based on a combination of semester work and a final exam. Semester work includes a quiz (25%) and a midterm exam (75%). The final grade is determined by the final exam (55%) and the in-year performance (45%).
